question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,1]\times [0,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2 \\ {x}^{3}+{y}^{3}-1\end{aligned}]. $$ Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[1,\,1]^{T},$ and compute the components of the first iteration, rounding your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).
$[$ {{field-1}} $2$ $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ {{field-2}} $]$
{{field-3}} $3$ $-1$
${x}_{1}≈[$ $0.833$ $]$
{{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be re-written as 

$$
{J}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+{y}^{3}-1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+{y}^{3}-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4x & 2y \\ 3{x}^{2} & 3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}4x & 2y \\ 3{x}^{2} & 3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2 \\ {x}^{3}+{y}^{3}-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}4x & 2y \\ 3{x}^{2} & 3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2 \\ {x}^{3}+{y}^{3}-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}4(1) & 2(1) \\ 3(1)^{2} & 3(1)^{2}\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}2(1)^{2}+(1)^{2}-2 \\ (1)^{3}+(1)^{3}-1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system of equations, we get $({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})=[\begin{aligned}-0.166\,66… \\ -0.166\,66…\end{aligned}].$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+[\begin{aligned}-0.166\,66… \\ -0.166\,66…\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-0.166\,66… \\ -0.166\,66…\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}0.833 \\ 0.833\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
